match.reason: The bank point covers both sexual and asexual reproduction and does not name the asexual methods (binary fission, budding, fragmentation, vegetative propagation) the new point teaches, so it is broader than the new point and would need new content rather than small changes.

draft.title: Asexual reproduction
card: In asexual reproduction, one parent produces offspring without gametes or fertilisation. The offspring are genetically identical to the parent, apart from rare mutations.
Binary fission
a single-celled organism, such as a bacterium, copies its DNA and splits into two cells.
Budding
a small outgrowth forms on the parent and detaches as a new individual. Yeast and hydra do this.
Fragmentation

a piece of the parent breaks off and grows into a new organism. Some sea stars and flatworms do this. In vegetative propagation, a plant grows new plants from parts such as runners or tubers, as strawberries and potatoes do.
draft.remember: One parent, no gametes, and offspring that are genetically identical to it.

a.q: Which feature is shared by all forms of asexual reproduction?
opts: One parent produces offspring with the same genes
Two parents each give half of the offspring's genes
The parent splits into two equal single cells
Offspring grow from a fertilised egg cell
a.why: All forms use one parent and give genetically identical offspring. Splitting into two equal cells is only binary fission, so it is not shared by budding or fragmentation.
a.clue: Think about what budding, fission and runners have in common.

b.q: Ravi plants one piece of a potato tuber and a new potato plant grows from it. Which statement is correct?
opts: It is vegetative propagation, and the new plant is identical
It is budding, and the new plant has genes from two parents
It is binary fission, and the new plant is identical
It is vegetative propagation, and the new plant is varied
b.why: A new plant grown from a part of one parent is vegetative propagation, and the offspring is genetically identical to that parent. Budding and binary fission are different processes, and no second parent is involved.
b.clue: A plant part grows into a whole plant, with only one parent.

a.best: One parent produces offspring with the same genes

b.best: It is vegetative propagation, and the new plant is identical

problems.detail: Vegetative propagation is placed inside the bullet that begins 'Fragmentation:', so a student could read it as a kind of fragmentation. It should have its own bullet, like the other three methods, especially since question b asks about it.

check.summary: The facts and both questions are correct. The one problem is that vegetative propagation sits inside the fragmentation bullet, which could make students think it is a type of fragmentation; it should have its own bullet.
